title: Accenture's Beat Sparks Rally Hopes for TCS, Infosys, Wipro Ahead of Monday's Reopen
excerpt: After Accenture's strong quarter and near-6% surges in Infosys and Wipro's US-listed shares, analysts expect a gap-up opening for Indian IT stocks on October 5 — but caution the pop may be short-lived.
body:
• Market experts expect Indian IT stocks to open sharply higher on Monday, October 5, following Accenture's better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results announced Wednesday.
  • Infosys and Wipro ADRs surged nearly 6% on the NYSE after the results, with analysts calling for a "gap-up" opening for TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCL Tech on Dalal Street.
  • Accenture beat earnings estimates by 11 cents ($3.29 per share) on revenue of $18.7 billion — up 6.3% year over year — with bookings rising 4% to $22.2 billion.
  • Analysts caution the pop may be short-lived: Nifty IT is still down 19% year to date, and experts advise booking profits after any intraday move above 5%.

Indian IT stocks are set for a strong opening when markets resume trading on Monday, October 5, as market experts expect the sector to rally on the back of Accenture's better-than-expected quarterly results. Shares of Infosys and Wipro listed on the New York Stock Exchange surged close to 6% after the announcement — a move analysts say signals a "gap-up" opening for the sector on Dalal Street.

The Catalyst: Accenture Beats, Raises the Bar

Accenture, the Dublin-headquartered IT services giant, reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $3.29 per share, beating analyst estimates by 11 cents. Revenue rose 6.3% year over year to $18.7 billion, exceeding expectations by roughly $660 million. Consulting revenue totalled $9.28 billion, while revenue from its communications, media and technology segment jumped 11% to $3.26 billion. Fourth-quarter bookings grew 4% year over year to $22.2 billion, pointing to resilient client spending on IT projects.

The numbers matter well beyond one company. Indian IT firms draw more than 50% of their revenue from the United States, and Accenture is widely treated as the sector's bellwether. "After the strong Accenture results, Indian IT stocks witnessed strong buying in the US stock market," said Avinash Gorakshkar, founder of Avinash Mentor Research. "Shares of Infosys and Wipro skyrocketed after the Accenture results, which is expected to fuel the positive sentiments about the Indian IT stocks of Dalal Street bulls."

What Analysts Expect Monday

"As the market has a track record of discounting events well before they take place, we can expect strong buying in Indian IT stocks on Monday," Gorakshkar said. Mahesh M Ojha, VP of Research and Business Development at KC Securities, echoed the call: "Indian IT companies draw more than 50% of their business from the US. Accenture plays a big role in it. So, we are bullish on IT stocks when trade resumes on Monday." Ojha picked Sagility, Birlasoft, Mphasis, Persistent Systems and LTIMindtree as the names likely to outperform when the market opens.

The move could also lift the broader benchmarks. IT stocks carry roughly 10% weight in the Nifty 50 and about 12% in the BSE Sensex, Gorakshkar noted, so a sector-wide rally would flow through to the headline indices.

A Rally Against a Weak Backdrop

The optimism arrives against a bruised year for the sector. The Nifty IT index is down nearly 19% year to date while the benchmark Nifty 50 is up about 5%. Clients have been cutting discretionary tech budgets, deal ramp-ups have slowed, and generative-AI fears have periodically hammered valuations. A weaker rupee — which hit an all-time low of ₹88.36 against the dollar recently — has cushioned margins, and earlier this week CLSA maintained "outperform" ratings on the majors, saying it saw no AI-led pricing pressure in deal renewals.

The Caution: Don't Chase It

Both experts quoted on the Monday call were quick to add a caveat: the rally may fizzle out. They advised investors to book profits rather than hold for the long term, suggesting shareholders take money off the table after an intraday gain of more than 5%.

"After the strong Accenture results, Indian IT stocks witnessed strong buying in the US stock market. Shares of Infosys and Wipro skyrocketed after the Accenture results."

— Avinash Gorakshkar, Founder, Avinash Mentor Research

What's Next

The real verdict comes with India's own earnings season. With Accenture's numbers raising expectations, all eyes shift to Q2 results from TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCL Tech over the coming weeks. If they confirm resilient demand and stabilising deal flows, Monday's gap-up could mark the start of a sustained recovery. If they disappoint, the rally will be remembered as a one-day wonder.
